name: Kyrgyz
variety: Standard Kyrgyz of Kyrgyzstan (northern dialect base), Cyrillic script
sources: Kara, Dávid Somfai (2003). Kyrgyz. Lincom Europa.
Kirchner, Mark (1998). Kirghiz. In Lars Johanson & Éva Á. Csató (eds.), The Turkic Languages. Routledge.
Hebert, Raymond J. & Poppe, Nicholas (1963). Kirghiz Manual. Indiana University.
contrasts: eight short vowels in a symmetrical system: high versus non-high, front versus back, rounded versus unrounded
phonemic vowel length, written with double letters (тоо 'mountain', суу 'water', жаан 'rain' versus жан 'soul'); long /iː ɯː/ are marginal
voiced versus voiceless stops and affricates
uvular [q ʁ] are variants of /k ɡ/ in back-vowel words, contrastive only in loans
strong rounding harmony: low vowels also round after rounded vowels, and the spelling shows it (көлдөр, тоолор)
allophony: /k/ is uvular [q] and /ɡ/ is [ʁ ~ ɢ] in back-vowel words; velar [k] and [ɡ ~ ɣ] in front-vowel words
/b/ is weakened to [β ~ w] between vowels
/q/ may be a fricative [χ] and /ɡ/ a fricative between vowels
word-initial ж is the affricate [dʒ]; [ʒ] occurs in Russian loans
suffix-initial consonants assimilate to the end of the stem (plural -лар, -дар, -тар with their harmonic variants)
/f v x ts/ occur in loanwords only; older loans replace f with p and x with k
phonotactics: no onset clusters in native words
coda clusters are sonorant + obstruent (төрт, кырк)
backness and rounding harmony throughout native words and suffixes; after /u/ a low suffix vowel stays unrounded /ɑ/ (куштар), after /o ø y/ it is rounded
long vowels and Russian loans may break harmony

stress.type: fixed final by default, with morphological exceptions
stress.rule: Stress falls on the last syllable of the word; unstressable suffixes and particles (negative -ба, question -бы, predicative personal endings) leave it on the syllable before them, and Russian loans may keep their own stress.
stress.cues: not instrumentally studied in the sources used; long vowels keep their length whether stressed or not

rhythm.vowel_reduction: none in quality; short high vowels can be very short between voiceless consonants

length.notes: Six long vowels /eː øː oː ɑː uː yː/ from the loss of consonants between vowels; they are written double. Geminates arise at morpheme boundaries and in a few stems. No published duration ratio is given here.

intonation.declarative: rise on the final stressed syllable of non-final phrases, fall at the end of the statement
intonation.yes_no_question: marked by the particle -бы (-би, -бу, -бү and variants with п); pitch is high on the syllable before the particle
intonation.wh_question: prominence on the question word, final fall
intonation.continuation: rise at the end of non-final phrases
intonation.accent_shape: rise to a high on the final stressed syllable
intonation.notes: Low confidence: no instrumental study of Kyrgyz intonation was available to me; the entries follow the general pattern of the better described Turkic languages (Turkish, Kazakh).

problems: the phoneme v (в) is defined as a vowel with vowel formants (a placeholder marked 'english v for now'), so в in loans such as вагон is not a fricative
ь and ъ are read as [j] (альбом gives [aljbom])
final stress is written into every vowel rule, so unstressable suffixes and particles are stressed (келдиби and келбейт get final stress)
dark l is changed to clear l before every vowel, so the velarised onset of back-vowel words is never produced
no weakening of b, g, q between vowels
the ipa strings of the table are not IPA (oe, N, S, X, tS, dZ, l-, t[), so --ipa output is wrong although the sounds are right
the statement and question tunes are the ones written for French (s3 c3 q3 e3)
good: long vowels from doubled letters, with about twice the length of short vowels
к and г become [q] and [ʁ] next to back vowels by rule
ж is [dʒ]; all eight vowel qualities are present and harmony follows from the spelling

notes: The consonant list includes /f v x ts/, which occur in loanwords only. The degree of aspiration of the voiceless stops is not documented in the sources used; eSpeak NG uses aspirated samples for p and k and an unaspirated dental t.
